covpp.coverage_planning.boustrophedon.cell_cov_planner module

Boustrophedon coverage path generation for decomposed trapezoidal cells.

class CellCoveragePathPlanner(cell: Cell, zone_ind: int = 0, resolution: float = 0.05)

Bases: object

Generate sweeping coverage paths for individual trapezoidal cells.

Creates alternating back-and-forth coverage paths within a decomposed cell by finding intersection points with horizontal scan lines.

Planning Process:

  1. Convert cell polygon to meter coordinates

  2. Find hitting points with cell boundary from top and bottom

  3. Connect hitting points in alternating boustrophedon pattern

  4. Convert final path to pixel coordinates

Parameters:

cell -- The trapezoidal cell to plan coverage for (from decomposition).

coverage_planning() → None

Execute boustrophedon path planning for the trapezoidal cell.

create_cell_polygon_in_meter() → bool

Convert cell polygon from pixel to meter coordinates and validate.

find_top_but_hit_points() → bool

Find hitting points with the cell polygon from top and bottom.

Process:

  1. Determine x-coordinates of vertical scan lines based on cell width and cleaning distance, adjusting for any shifts.

  2. For each x-coordinate, create a vertical line from above the cell downwards and find intersection points with the cell polygon.

  3. Store the bottom and top intersection points for path generation.

class CoveragePathPlanner(cell: PCell, zmd: ZoneMapData)

Bases: CoveragePathPlannerBase

Coverage path planner using boustrophedon (back-and-forth) decomposition.

Basic input data for the planner is MapPolygons object created from cell.map. cell.map boundary is either original cell polygon or inscribed rectangle.

This planner creates parallel sweeping paths by decomposing the cell into trapezoidal regions and generating alternating scan lines.

Pipeline Steps:

  1. Create map polygons for cell workspace

  2. Decompose cell into boustrophedon sub-cells

  3. Plan coverage path for each sub-cell

  4. Rotate paths back to original orientation

  5. Connect all sub-cell paths into complete coverage

Result:

Sets path_m and path_px attributes for the cell.

class CellDecomposition(main_cell_id, resolution: float = 0.05, results_dir: str = None)

Bases: object

Perform new trapezoidal decomposition for boustrophedon path planning.

This class decomposes a workspace into trapezoidal cells suitable for parallel sweeping coverage patterns, handles cell adjacency, and merges compatible cells for efficient coverage.

Decomposition Pipeline:

  1. Create obstacles and events

  2. Decompose into trapezoidal cells

  3. Find adjacent cells

  4. Complete adjacency relationships

  5. Create cell groups and merge compatible cells

  6. Set merged cell adjacency

  7. Evaluate cells for planning requirements

  8. Visualize decomposition results

initiate()

Execute complete decomposition pipeline.

Runs all steps from obstacle creation through visualization of the final decomposed cells.

set_bounding_polygon(poly: Polygon)

Set the workspace boundary polygon.

set_obstacle_polygons(polygons: list[Polygon])

Set the list of obstacle polygons within the workspace.

create_obstacles()
create_events()
add_cell(poly: Polygon, event: Event)
decompose_all()

Decompose all the events to create trapezoidal cells.

Steps:

1- Iterate over all events (skip skip_sweep and done events). 2- For each event, find hits by sweeping line (up and down) (sweep_up_down). 3- Evaluate done status of hit events (eval_done_status). 4- Create trapezoids based on event type and hits (create_trapezoid).

sweep_up_down(base_e: Event, base_i: int)

Sweep line from the base event to find hit events.

Method:

1- Iterate over events after the base event. 2- For each event, evaluate if it can be hit (eval_event_up and eval_event_down). 3- Update hit variables if successful. 4- Return hit results.

eval_event_up(base_e: Event, e: Event, y_hit: float) → bool

Evaluate if event e can be hit when sweeping up from base_e.

Method: 1- Check if e is of type 'up' 2- Check if e is not hit from outside of polygon 3- Check for higher 'updown' events with same x coordinate 4- Evaluate if sweep line hits the edge formed by e and its previous event based on coordinates 5- Return success status and new hit y-coordinate if successful

eval_event_down(base_e: Event, e: Event, y_hit: float) → bool

Evaluate if event e can be hit when sweeping down from base_e.

Method: 1- Check if e is of type 'down' 2- Evaluate if sweep line hits the edge formed by e and its next event based on coordinates 3- Return success status and new hit y-coordinate if successful

eval_done_status(base_e: Event, hit_up_event: Event, hit_down_event: Event)

Evaluate done status of hit events.

Method: 1- Evaluate events on the same x coordinate between base_e and hit_up_event 2- Update done status of the hit events

create_trapezoid(base_e: Event, hit_up_event: Event, hit_down_event: Event)

Create trapezoids based on event type and hits.

Method: 1- Handle direct trap case. 2- Handle not hit events case. 3- Create trapezoids based on event type (updown, up, down). 4- Add cell number and update endpoints of hit events. 5- Create cell(s) and add to the list.

Trapezoid vertex are: base_e, base_e_hit (up or down), hit_event endpoint, base_e endpoint

find_adjacents_cells()

Find adjacent cells based on hit events.

Method: 1- Iterate over all events. 2- Find adjacents based on hit_up_event and hit_down_event. 3- Update adjacent and parent cell indices for the involved cells.

complete_adjacency()

Complete adjacency by checking geometric conditions.

Method: 1- Iterate over all cells. 2- For each cell, check for potential adjacent cells on the right side.

  • Compare x_max of the current cell with x_min of the next cell.

  • Check y-overlap conditions.

3- If conditions are met, add adjacent and parent relationships.

create_cell_groups()

Create cell groups and merged cells. Procedure:

1- Iterate over all cells. 2- For each ungrouped cell, create a new group. 3- If the base cell has multiple adjacents, only add it to the group (no adjacents added). 4- If the base cell has a single adjacent, traverse through adjacents

and add them to the group until a cell with multiple adjacents or a grouped cell is reached.

5- After forming the group, update group properties (first and last cell) and store the merged cell.

set_merged_cells_adjacents()

Set merged cells adjacents based on cell groups (first and last cell).

class Obstacle(ind: int, poly: Polygon)

Bases: object

Encapsulate a polygonal obstacle and its decomposition events.

Each obstacle generates a sequence of sweep-line events that drive the trapezoidal decomposition. The class pre-processes vertices, injects fake events for vertical edges, and evaluates event types (up/down/in/out) used by CellDecomposition.
